newsitem.title: UK: Canada greets delay on Nigeria sanctions move.
newsitem.headline: Canada greets delay on Nigeria sanctions move.

text.p: Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy on Wednesday welcomed a Commonwealth decision to once again delay imposing sanctions on Nigeria, saying the 53-nation body needed more information before reaching a conclusion.

Axworthy has consistently pressed for sanctions against Nigeria, which was suspended from the Commonwealth in 1995 after it executed author Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other human rights activists, but he has had to modify his stance in the face of opposition from other members of the grouping.

On Tuesday the eight-nation Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG) invited written submissions from interested parties before it reports to a Commonwealth summit in Edinburgh this October on what should be done about Nigeria.
"We were very pleased that the consensus was to open up the agenda to a wide variety of people," Axworthy told a news conference in London.
CMAG came under heavy fire from opposition groups last year when it sent a fact-finding delegation to Abuja which only met officials from the military government of General Sani Abacha.
"There was a lot of debate over the CMAG trip to Nigeria and what we were anxious to see was that it (the report on the visit) was not the only document to be presented at Edinburgh," Axworthy said.
"We have to get a broad representation of views to see what is happening in Nigeria. The delegation didn't have that opportunity and that's what we were worried about," he said.
CMAG decided last year to impose a number of limited sanctions on Nigeria.
But the eight-nation action group is deeply split over what measures to take against the oil-rich west African nation and has repeatedly voted to delay imposing the sanctions.
Axworthy said CMAG would invite some of those who made written submissions to speak to the action group in July.
"Anyone who wants to submit, submits...the Nigerian opposition certainly has the right to submit and the right to be heard," he said.
Some Commonwealth ministers have already said that Nigeria should be expelled if it does not make more progress towards restoring democracy, holding elections and freeing jailed opposition leaders.

Axworthy said he had his own views on what should be done but declined to elaborate. "The fact that an agreement has been made to invite all submissions is very helpful and I don't want to jeopardise it by saying I have already concluded what should be done," he said.
CMAG comprises Canada, Britain, New Zealand, South Africa, Jamaica, Malaysia, Ghana and Zimbabwe.
